digest.component_or_area: LLM provider integration — first-class AWS Bedrock support with native prompt caching
propositions: Rebar has no native Bedrock provider; clients requiring Bedrock must currently use an OpenAI-compatible gateway proxy, which sacrifices prompt caching, retrying transport, and native structured output.

Bedrock prompt caching is model-dependent and fails silently — some inference profiles (e.g., claude-opus-4-5) report zero cache tokens while billing full input on every call, with no error or warning.

Temperature sampling parameters hard-fail (400 ValidationException) on specific Bedrock models (e.g., claude-opus-4-7 rejects temperature=0), but pydantic-ai's Bedrock leaf lacks the _drop_unsupported_sampling_settings guard present in its Anthropic leaf, breaking rebar's Pass-2 verify gates that deliberately send temperature=0 for greedy determinism.

The direct-Anthropic path sets exactly two cache keys (anthropic_cache_instructions and anthropic_cache_tool_definitions) for parity; Bedrock must set exactly the same two (bedrock_cache_instructions and bedrock_cache_tool_definitions), not a third (bedrock_cache_messages), to maintain measured parity.
On-demand Bedrock model IDs are not invokable in production infrastructure; only inference-profile ARNs work, requiring documentation and runtime validation to prevent silent billing anomalies.

Rebar's runner.py and providers.py are at or above their attested LOC caps, so new Bedrock construction logic must live in a separate leaf module (bedrock_model.py) without breaching signed criteria or blocking dependent stories requiring headroom.
